text.tspan: Everyday English - B2 - 2026/06/06 - Essay - 01
Hands cultivate a garden with care.
Pexels · 7729129
Growing something small
A good way to care for a plant combines practical structure with an awareness of other people. Neither a rigid plan nor complete improvisation
is sufficient on its own; both need to be judged in context.
The practical case is straightforward: observing a plant helps us respond to what it needs. Consider how we check whether the soil feels dry
before adding water. The benefit is not merely efficiency. A modest arrangement prevents avoidable confusion, leaving attention available for
the activity itself rather than for problems that could have been anticipated.
Consideration adds a second, equally important dimension: keeping a simple record helps us learn from changes. In this situation, we note
which window gives the plant enough light without scorching its leaves. A decision can be convenient for one person while creating difficulty
for another, so its value depends partly on whose needs it recognises.
The most useful approach therefore brings structure and consideration together. Preparation establishes a workable starting point; attention to
other people keeps it responsive. Success should be assessed by how well the arrangement serves the experience, rather than by how
closely events follow the original plan.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a clear main idea; develop two different points with examples; bring them together in the conclusion. Each body
paragraph needs a distinct point and a concrete example. The conclusion should connect the argument rather than introduce a new proposal.
Compare two ways to care for a plant: a rigid plan and one that allows adjustment. Assess one advantage and one limitation. Use four short
paragraphs: introduction, two developed points, and conclusion. (Model: One possible outline: introduce the situation; discuss observing a
plant helps us respond to what it needs with an example; discuss keeping a simple record helps us learn from changes with a different
example; conclude by connecting the two points.)
